author: Mary Ellen Haney East Fairmont Community Correspondent
title: Antibiotics are marvelous things! | Harrison County Columns | wvnews.com
text:
There is a Dutch proverb that speaks to my frame of mind as well as to my achy body this week: “Sickness comes on horseback but departs on foot.”
Pneumonia galloped into my house at the end of July, and I don’t think it’s fair to be sick during the summer, which is flying by as it always does. Fair or not, I returned from visiting my daughter and her family in Indiana and brought along an unwelcome guest.
The first week was spent sleeping the clock around, coughing, drinking copious amounts of hot tea and taking multiple cold-relief meds. On the first day of the second week, I finally did the intelligent thing and visited urgent care. Following a breathing treatment and a chest X-ray, I learned that pneumonia had invaded my right lung.
Samuel Butler once opined that “I reckon being ill is one of the great pleasures of life, provided one is not too ill and is not obliged to work till one is better.” Fortunately, I’m retired from the five-day work week, and very grateful not to be “too ill” and able to recover at home until pneumonia decides to trot slowly away.
By the way, antibiotics are marvelous things!
